note: Fixed tips per confusion pair (target -> produced), never generated at request time. LLM-drafted (Claude); reviewed: true once a human reviewer approved it (see REVIEWED). Facts come from content/articulation.json; the LLM is never used for these.

r_as_l.what_happened: In “{word}”, the R probably sounded like an L.
r_as_l.tip: Pull your tongue back and don't let the tip touch the roof of your mouth. Round your lips slightly.

l_as_r.what_happened: In “{word}”, the L probably sounded like an R.
l_as_r.tip: Touch the ridge just behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip and keep it there as the vowel starts. Don't curl the tongue back.

f_as_p.what_happened: In “{word}”, the F probably sounded like a P.
f_as_p.tip: Rest your upper teeth lightly on your lower lip and blow a long “fff”. Your lips never close for F.

v_as_b.what_happened: In “{word}”, the V probably sounded like a B.
v_as_b.tip: Upper teeth on your lower lip like F, but turn your voice on so it buzzes: “vvv”. Don't press your lips together.

th_as_s.what_happened: In “{word}”, the TH probably sounded like an S or T.
th_as_s.tip: Put your tongue tip lightly between your front teeth and blow. Don't press, and don't pull the tip back behind the teeth like for S.

dh_as_d.what_happened: In “{word}”, the TH probably sounded like a D.
dh_as_d.tip: Tongue tip lightly between your front teeth, voice on, and let the air keep flowing so it buzzes. If the tip presses the ridge, it becomes D.

ih_as_iy.what_happened: In “{word}”, the short i probably sounded like a long ee.
ih_as_iy.tip: Relax: let your tongue and jaw drop a little from the “ee” position, and keep the vowel short. Ship is shorter and looser than sheep.

iy_as_ih.what_happened: In “{word}”, the long ee probably sounded like a short i.
iy_as_ih.tip: Spread your lips like a small smile, push your tongue high and forward, and hold the vowel a little longer: “sheeep”.

extra_vowel.what_happened: “{word}” probably had an extra “eu” vowel after the last sound.
extra_vowel.tip: End the word on the consonant and stop your voice right there. Don't release it into a small “eu”.

word_not_heard.what_happened: We couldn't hear “{word}” in your recording.
word_not_heard.tip: Say every word, including short ones like “a”, “the” and “to”. Try again a little slower.

eo_as_o.what_happened: In “{word}”, ㅓ probably sounded like ㅗ.
eo_as_o.tip: Keep your lips relaxed and open, not rounded or pushed forward, and drop your jaw a bit more than for ㅗ. The tongue stays back for both.

eu_as_u.what_happened: In “{word}”, ㅡ probably sounded like ㅜ.
eu_as_u.tip: Keep the tongue high and back as for ㅜ, but spread your lips flat like a slight smile. No rounding at all.

ae_as_e.what_happened: In “{word}”, ㅐ may have sounded like ㅔ.
ae_as_e.tip: Open your jaw a little more than for ㅔ. Many Seoul speakers say ㅐ and ㅔ the same (they've merged), so this is a fine detail.

tap_as_r.what_happened: In “{word}”, ㄹ probably sounded like an English R.
tap_as_r.tip: Don't curl your tongue back. Flick the tip once, quickly, against the ridge behind your upper teeth, like the tt in American “butter”.

tap_as_l.what_happened: In “{word}”, ㄹ probably sounded like a long English L.
tap_as_l.tip: Between vowels, touch the ridge for only an instant and let go right away. Don't hold the tongue there like an English L.

pp_as_p.what_happened: In “{word}”, you probably said a plain ㅂ where the word needs a tense ㅃ.
pp_as_p.tip: Tighten your throat, press your lips firmly, and release with no puff of air. Start the vowel high and sharp.

pp_as_ph.what_happened: In “{word}”, you probably said an aspirated ㅍ (too much air) where the word needs a tense ㅃ.
pp_as_ph.tip: Hold a hand in front of your mouth: for ㅃ you should feel almost no air. Tighten your throat and release the lips without a puff.

ph_as_p.what_happened: In “{word}”, you probably said a plain ㅂ where the word needs an aspirated ㅍ.
ph_as_p.tip: Release your lips with a big puff of air (you can feel it on your hand) and start the vowel at a high pitch.

p_as_ph.what_happened: In “{word}”, you probably said an aspirated ㅍ where the word needs a plain ㅂ.
p_as_ph.tip: Use a lighter puff and start the vowel at a lower, relaxed pitch. In Seoul speech, the vowel's pitch is a big part of what separates ㅂ from ㅍ.
